DanCrab · source-derived experiment

GRVQ ansatz comparison

Exact optimizer · Numerical reference diagnostics

336 completed runs compare 7 ansatz families on 16 finite objective models. The report separates exact computation from numerical reference metrics and shows the observed R2/R4 tradeoff.

Observed run created 2026-11-22T11:53:25.538582+00:00. Source snapshot e7aca179d2a492769a1f2dfb8e5b4f56e9b58fa0.

16declared objective models
336complete optimization runs
129,360exact objective evaluations
29 / 29methods used in coefficient generation

What the comparison establishes

Most per-model median wins in this run: R4 + reversed order (5 model wins), GRVQ R2 product (4 model wins), R2 + controlled Cayley (4 model wins). This count describes only the selected benchmark set.

Ranking uses the exact median Rayleigh energy within each model. Models have different scales and interpretations, so raw energies are not pooled across models. Every run uses 385 objective evaluations and the declared seeds 7, 19, 43. Parameter counts differ between families and are reported below.

Optimization ran locally using exact classical state simulation. The recorded qBraid work, when present, independently checks selected optimized exported circuits and measurement energies; it does not execute the full training loop.

Paired signs above are computed from exact rational energies. Error and fidelity columns use a numerical eigensystem reference.

Median objective error

Each cell uses the median across the declared seeds. The color is log10(max(abs(E−E0),10⁻¹⁵)); the floor affects only this display.

PNG · SVG

Convergence under the same objective budget

Lines are median incumbent energy gaps. Shading is the minimum-to-maximum seed range, not a confidence interval. Numerical absolute-gap display floor: 10⁻¹⁵.

PNG · SVG

Paired R4−R2 energy differences

Negative values favor R4; positive values favor R2. Each model and seed is paired at the same budget. Points are medians; bars show the seed range. The axis is symmetric logarithmic.

PNG · SVG

Runtime and final objective error

Every point is one complete optimization run. Runtime is measured wall time for the exact optimizer. This is a small-system implementation comparison, not a quantum speedup measurement.

PNG · SVG

All 29 methods in the coefficient compiler

Actual function-entry counts in the source compiler that generates the simulation coefficients. Call counts establish execution, not accuracy or a performance advantage.

PNG · SVG

Measured cost of conventional exact replacements

Points show median coefficient-generation milliseconds and bars span the observed minimum and maximum across randomized repetition blocks. The vertical line is the original source median. Process startup, source loading and instrumentation are excluded. These measurements describe this compiler workload and machine.

Conventional exact arithmetic controls

30 of 30 observed compiler variants produced exactly identical mathematical outputs. The variants replace each consumed polynomial extension individually and all 29 together with conventional exact algorithms. Equivalent coefficient arithmetic therefore produces the same model; it does not create a new ground energy. The reported equality holds across 9 repetitions per variant.

The unchanged source median is 31.783 ms. A ratio below one means the conventional replacement compiled this workload faster. The ratio is the conventional median divided by the unchanged-source median; all raw timings and randomized block orders are retained.

Complete control results and call counts

Source selection and the update

The audit selects grvq_canonical.py and grvq_book_chain.py as the strongest recent exact source foundation. The benchmark develops the separately authored product construction in Untitled5.ipynb: Ψᵢ = fᵢ Rₚ(rᵢ) ∏ⱼ(1+αⱼSⱼ(xᵢ)). These scalar families are distinct, and this experiment does not assert that the product equals the canonical transcendental expression.

The defined radial factor is Rₚ(r) = ∏ⱼ λⱼᵖ / (rᵖ + λⱼᵖ), with p=2 or p=4. Both variants use the same declared shell widths. The four-shell R2 is a matched control constructed for this experiment; it extends the source notebook's single-shell R2. Exact rational controlled Cayley rotations are added and tested in forward, reversed, and local-only variants. The four shape polynomials are actual cardinal polynomials generated by the source coefficient compiler, and the carrier is the nonconstant interpolant of 1+x.

  • dns/vedic-polynomial.js and dns/vedic-operators.js supply the arithmetic and consumed polynomial extensions.
  • ansatz.py supplies the H/Ry/CZ circuit lineage. The experiment baseline explicitly uses two layers and a ring, with exact rational Cayley parameters.
  • The update is a declared finite variational experiment. Its explicit shape functions, shell widths, potentials, and couplings are experiment inputs, not inferred universal constants.

Metric definitions

Exact computation

Energy is (ψᵀAψ)/(ψᵀMψ). Ordinary models use M=I; the spectral problems retain their exact mass matrix. Candidate comparisons and accepted optimizer updates use rational arithmetic. Original state vectors, parameters, matrices, and every objective evaluation are retained.

For ordinary models, exact energy variance is ||Hψ−Eψ||²/||ψ||². This tests eigenstate quality independently of energy reduction.

Numerical diagnostics

The ground-energy reference is scipy.linalg.eigh(A,M) applied to a numerical projection of the exact matrices. Ground-subspace fidelity sums overlaps over the complete numerically identified degenerate ground space, using the mass metric. Each model records its reference residual and eigenspace tolerance.

Plots, displayed decimals, fidelity, generalized residual diagnostics, and exported QASM angles are numerical boundary outputs. Log plots use a stated display-only floor.

Scope of the result

  • The measured conclusions apply to these finite matrices, declared initializations, ansatz families, and optimization budgets. They do not establish universal superiority of R4, all Vedic methods, or a quantum speed advantage.
  • Exact arithmetic proves the represented operations are not rounded; it does not by itself prove the continuum physics, an optimizer's global convergence, or a runtime-to-Lean refinement.
  • The polynomial identities and conventional controls compare arithmetic implementations of the same model. Equivalent exact identities should agree on coefficients and objective values.
  • Q4, toroidal, and finite-grid models are defined experiments. Spin models use explicit Pauli conventions. No molecular H₂ result is asserted.
  • All seeds and families are shown. Wall time is measured for this implementation and machine; sample ranges are descriptive rather than statistical confidence intervals.
